newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Cie Bancaire to buy out units.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Cie Bancaire to buy out units.

text.p: In a bid to boost profits, French specialist retail financial services firm Cie Bancaire announced plans on Wednesday to buy out its two units, Cardif and UFB Locabail, for a maximum three billion francs ($515 million).

Shares of Cie Bancaire, majority-owned by financial group Paribas, climbed by 6.69 percent to 734 francs by early afternoon as brokers upgraded their earnings estimates for the company. Shares of Paribas rose 4.62 percent to 405 francs.
A Cie Bancaire spokeswoman said the transactions were aimed at "accelarating the improvement in its profitability".
Cie Bancaire has been aiming for 15 percent return on equity in the medium term, up from 10 percent currently.
Cie Bancaire said it would offer 900 francs per share for the 39.4 percent of Cardif in public hands and 600 francs for the 27.5 percent of UFB Locabail in the market.
Cardif finances business equipment while UFB Locabail is involved insurance and savings.
Cie Bancaire said it was considering a maximum two billion franc capital increase before year-end to finance the bids. It said Paribas would subscribe 50 percent to the capital boost.
Shares of Cardif closed at 655 francs on Tuesday while shares of UFB Locabail closed at 522 francs.

Cie Bancaire said the price proposed for Cardif stock represented a 26 percent premium over the average trading price in the past three months, while the price for UFB Locabail offered a 13 percent premium over the past three months.
Cie Bancaire said it would merge with Cardif following completion of the bid.
Paribas announced in May it had lifted its stake in Cie Bancaire to 50.28 percent to consolidate its hold over the company which is the centrepiece of its specialist financial services activities.
The Paribas group's other core business is international investment holdings.
UFB Locabail recorded a 1996 net attributable profit of 225 million francs. Cardif's profit totalled 340.1 million francs.

Cie Bancaire, which last year recorded a 1.23 billion franc loss due to provisions to cover exposure to risky property activities, said it had to carry 100 percent of the losses of its troubled property companies. By contrast it could only integrate part of the profits of its listed subsidiaries.

"By increasing the contribution of Cardif and UFB Locabail to Cie Bancaire's consolidated net profit, the proposed transactions will raise Cie Bancaire's net profit," the bank said in a statement. ($ = 5.824 French Francs)
